_readme: FREE PLAY presets, in the order they appear on the menu.
THE WHOLE MENU SHIFTED UP. Six presets starting at a 2-room house was too
many decisions for a mode you pick when you just want to tidy something,
and the small end went unplayed — free play is where you go for a big one.
The two smallest were dropped and the rest relabelled, so "Small" here is
a 4-room house, not a starter one.
`id` DELIBERATELY NO LONGER MATCHES `label`. The id is written into saves
(`size`), so renaming ids would orphan every run in progress; the label is
the only part players see. Add new presets with fresh ids and never reuse
an old one for different numbers.
There is deliberately NO item count here. The real number is
targetTypes x rowLen, and the menu computes and shows that — so it can
never drift out of sync the way the old hardcoded '~50 items' labels did.
rooms       — how many rooms to grow (max 9: the layout is a 3x3 grid)
targetTypes — how many distinct emoji the run uses (max = total types in the
theme's rooms; boot validation checks this)
rowLen      — items per row, i.e. how many of each emoji exist
doorLocks   — how many doors are sealed;  doorKeys = keys needed per door
contLocks   — how many containers are locked; contKeys = keys needed per container
caches      — hidden coin-slot boxes holding items taken off the floor
junk        — start some containers with foreign clutter to drag out
scale       — [min,max] random room size, 1 = fills the stage
theme       — which world this preset draws from (data/themes.json)
group       — the heading this preset sits under in the menu. Presets with
the same group are listed together and the heading is printed
once, in first-appearance order.
FREE PLAY IS WHERE PEOPLE GO FOR A BIG ONE, and until the worlds landed it
was four house presets and nothing else — the campaign could take you to a
ship and a tower and free play could not. Every world now has an entry, so
the menu is 'where' as much as 'how big'. The four house sizes keep their
ids and their order because the id is written into saves.
targetTypes ON A WORLD PRESET IS DELIBERATELY ABOUT HALF ITS POOL. Each of
the new worlds holds roughly 150 types across six rooms, and asking for all
of them would make every run of that world the same run. Asking for half
means the six rooms drawn, and the containers drawn inside them, differ every
time — which is the entire point of building the worlds in the first place.
The ceiling is still real: boot validation refuses more types than the
n-largest rooms can hold, so raise the room count before raising this.

sizes._note: One preset per world. Sized so a run uses most of a small pool rather than a slice of a big one — see the ceiling note above.
sizes.label: Frat House

sizes._note: The dream pool is only four rooms, so this one always draws all of them. It has been playable in the campaign since D-1 and reachable from free play never, which was an oversight rather than a decision.
sizes.label: The Dream
